claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially homogenized as a high-temperature disordered BCC phase.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between composition-induced thermodynamic instability and kinetic limitations on atomic rearrangement.
Decreasing temperature makes the target alloy's disordered BCC phase thermodynamically unstable.
The proposed thermodynamic instability favors transformation from disordered BCC/A2 to ordered B2 in the target alloy.
A2 is a disordered BCC phase and B2 is an ordered BCC phase.
Formation of the ordered state requires sufficient atomic diffusion and mobility.
Slow cooling permits enough atomic rearrangement for ordering in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Rapid quenching suppresses ordering and retains a metastable, predominantly disordered BCC state in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The ordered-phase fraction increases as cooling rate decreases.
Slight compositional fluctuations may promote secondary-phase nucleation during ordering.
New superlattice peaks or peak splitting would identify B2 ordering in the proposed diffraction experiment.
At sufficiently low cooling rates, additional secondary phases may approach their equilibrium state.
The hypothesis assumes that segregation and impurities have minimal influence during processing.
Rapidly quenched and slowly cooled specimens of the same composition provide the controlled comparison.
The rapidly quenched specimen is the baseline against which ordering in slowly cooled specimens is compared.
Failure of slow cooling to increase ordering significantly over the quenched baseline, or observation of ordering independent of cooling rate, would falsify the proposed kinetic modulation.

contradictions.description: The rapid-quench baseline is explicitly intended to freeze in the metastable disordered BCC state, but the boundary states that the hypothesis applies only at cooling rates that are not so high as to completely freeze in that state. Thus, the principal baseline is nominally outside the stated applicability range.
